messages:
casey: Heads-up — eu-west-1 gpu nodepool is starved. ~80 Pending GPU pods, autoscaler logs show suppressed scaling.
infra-bot: ALERT: cluster-autoscaler suppressed scaling for nodegroup gpu-eu-west1-spot: insufficient IPs in subnet (ENI quota).
ana: (typo)
ana: ---
ana: wait ignore
ana: I'm jumping in. casey can you paste the pending pod list?
casey: kubectl get pods -n batch -o wide | grep Pending
casey: batch-eval-0001   Pending   0/1 gpu   nodeSelector: gpu=true   requests: 1gpu
casey: batch-eval-0002   Pending   0/1 gpu
casey: ... (~80 more)
marco: @casey @ana scheduler note: saw a sudden fanout from CI, roughly 500 parallel tasks spawned by a nightly job with parallelism=500. That explains the burst.
li: AWS console shows ENI usage spike in eu-west-1a, subnet subnet-0a had /24 and is at ~98% IPs used.
sarah-oncall: Proposed mitigations: 1) pause offending CI job, 2) create an emergency on-demand nodegroup, 3) expand subnet or move nodegroup to larger subnet.
casey: Pausing CI now: POST internal-ci/api/cancel?job=batch-nightly — response 200, canceling active runners.
casey: Creating temporary on-demand nodegroup: aws-nodegroups create --cluster redwood-eu --name gpu-eu-od-temp --instance-type p4d.12xlarge --count 6
infra-bot: Deploybot: nodegroup gpu-eu-od-temp created (status: pending).
li: I requested a subnet resize (create second /24 -> attach /23) — AWS says ~4–6 minutes for provisioning in that AZ.
marco: Short-term: we can evict low-priority batch pods to free GPUs. Run eviction for pods with priorityClass=batch-low?
ana: (correcting earlier typo)
ana: please run evict.
casey: kubectl delete pod -l job=batch,priority=batch-low -n batch --grace-period=0 --force
casey: Evicted ~120 low-priority pods, freed ~40 GPUs. Autoscaler still hitting provider 429s though.
casey: Console API for scaling on-demand returned 202 then 429 a few times; retried and nodes are now reporting Ready (3 of 6).
sarah-oncall: Good — start draining spot nodes to free IPs and reduce pod churn.
marco: Also setting a taint to prevent new batch pods landing on spot pool: kubectl taint nodes -l nodepool=spot-gpu spot-evict=true:NoSchedule
casey: Done. Also patched batch CI config to reduce parallelism to 20 pending per runner.
li: Subnet /23 attach completed. ENI counts are dropping, autoscaler resumed normal behavior.
infra-bot: NOTICE: cluster-autoscaler scaling resumed for nodegroup gpu-eu-west1-spot.
casey: Manual scaling steps (temporary): patched nodegroup desired capacity via console due to API throttling. Nodes joined, pods scheduling.
sarah-oncall: Cost impact note: emergency on-demand nodegroup ~ +$7k/day while active. Tagging incident-cost:incident-1761117777.
marco: Root cause summary: misconfigured CI parallelism triggered a large fanout -> exhausted subnet IPs (ENI quota) -> autoscaler suppressed scaling.
casey: Action items: [1] increase default subnet size for gpu nodepools in eu-west, [2] add CI rate-limiter or concurrency cap, [3] add preemptible capacity guard to avoid full exhaustion, [4] automate on-demand fallback runbook.
ana: assigning owners: @marco scheduler change, @li network/subnet sizing, @casey runbook and playbook update.
sarah-oncall: I'll open the incident postmortem and schedule a follow-up with infra and CI teams. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: RESOLVED: gpu-pool-starvation auto-resolved at 1761117950.
casey: Thanks everyone.
